concept: sin and cos on the unit circle
prompt:
The point $P(-0.6,\ 0.8)$ lies on the unit circle and $OP$ makes an angle $\theta$ with the positive $x$-axis.

**(a)** Write down $\cos\theta$ and $\sin\theta$. **[2]**

**(b)** Write down $\sin(\pi-\theta)$. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\cos\theta=-0.6$, $\sin\theta=0.8$ (the $x$- and $y$-coordinates) **(A2)**

**(b)** The angle $\pi-\theta$ gives the point reflected in the $y$-axis, $(0.6,0.8)$, so $\sin(\pi-\theta)=0.8$ **(A1)**

concept: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ
prompt:
**(a)** The point $P(-0.6,0.8)$ lies on the unit circle at angle $\theta$. Find $\tan\theta$. **[1]**

**(b)** Explain why $\tan\dfrac\pi2$ is undefined. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\tan\theta=\dfrac{0.8}{-0.6}=-\dfrac43$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $\cos\dfrac\pi2=0$, so $\dfrac{\sin(\pi/2)}{\cos(\pi/2)}$ involves division by zero **(R1)** (the graph has a vertical asymptote there).

$\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}=\dfrac12$, $\cos\dfrac{4\pi}{3}=-\dfrac12$, $\tan\dfrac{3\pi}{4}=-1$ **(A2)** (A1 for two correct)

Sum $=-1$ **(A1)**

Use the reference angle and the quadrant's signs: e.g. $\frac{4\pi}{3}$ is in the third quadrant, where cosine is negative.

concept: The ambiguous case of the sine rule
prompt:
In triangle $ABC$, $a=7$ cm, $b=9$ cm and $A=40^{\circ}$.

**(a)** Show that there are two possible triangles. **[3]**

**(b)** Find the two possible values of $c$. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\sin B=\dfrac{9\sin40^{\circ}}{7}=0.826$ **(M1)**, so $B=55.7^{\circ}$ or $B=124.3^{\circ}$ **(A1)**. Both satisfy $A+B<180^{\circ}$, so both give valid triangles **(R1)**.

**(b)** $C=84.3^{\circ}$: $c=\dfrac{7\sin84.3^{\circ}}{\sin40^{\circ}}=10.8$ cm; $C=15.7^{\circ}$: $c=2.95$ cm **(A1)(A1)**

Ambiguity arises when the given angle is opposite the **shorter** of the two given sides.
